challenge the decision: The players were angry about the referee's call, so their coach decided to challenge the decision after the game.
球員對裁判的判決很不滿，所以教練決定在賽後質疑這個決定。
challenge authority: Teenagers often challenge authority by asking their parents and teachers why they must follow certain rules.
青少年常常藉由詢問父母和老師為什麼必須遵守某些規定來挑戰權威。
challenge someone to a game: After practicing chess every night for a month, I finally challenged my best friend to a game.
每晚練習西洋棋一個月後，我終於向我最好的朋友挑戰比賽。
challenge assumptions: Good scientists always challenge assumptions instead of simply accepting what most people already believe is true.
優秀的科學家總會質疑假設，而不是單純接受大多數人早已相信的事。
champion human rights: The lawyer has spent thirty years trying to champion human rights for workers who are treated unfairly.
這位律師花了三十年為受到不公平對待的勞工捍衛人權。
champion a cause: Many young people use social media to champion a cause they care about, such as protecting the ocean.
許多年輕人利用社群媒體擁護他們在乎的理念，例如保護海洋。
champion the underdog: The reporter is known to champion the underdog, telling the stories of poor families that nobody else listens to.
這位記者以為弱者發聲聞名，報導那些沒人願意傾聽的貧困家庭的故事。
channel energy into: Instead of playing video games all day, he decided to channel his energy into training for the school marathon.
他決定把精力投入為學校馬拉松做訓練，而不是整天打電動。
channel funds: The city government plans to channel funds from the new tax into building more parks and libraries.
市政府計畫將新稅收的資金引導到興建更多公園和圖書館。
channel one's anger: The coach taught the boy to channel his anger into hard training rather than fighting with other players.
教練教這個男孩把怒氣疏導到努力訓練上，而不是和其他球員打架。
through official channels: If you want to complain about your grade, you should do it through official channels instead of posting online.
如果你想對成績提出申訴，應該透過正式管道，而不是在網路上發文。
be characterized by: Taiwan's summer is characterized by hot weather, heavy afternoon rain, and frequent typhoons.
台灣的夏天以炎熱的天氣、午後大雨和頻繁的颱風為特色。
characterize someone as: Most of her classmates would characterize her as a kind and hard-working student who always helps others.
她大多數的同學會把她形容為一個善良又用功、總是幫助別人的學生。
characterize the era: Rapid changes in technology and the rise of smartphones characterize the era we are living in today.
科技的快速變化和智慧型手機的興起代表了我們現今生活的那個時代。
charge a fee: The museum is free on Sundays, but it will charge a fee of 200 dollars on other days.
博物館星期日免費，但其他日子會收取兩百元的費用。
charge someone with murder: After finding his fingerprints on the knife, the police decided to charge the man with murder.
在刀上發現他的指紋後，警方決定以謀殺罪控告這名男子。
charge the battery: My phone is almost dead, so I need to charge the battery before we leave for the concert.
我的手機快沒電了，所以出發去演唱會前我需要充電。
take charge of: When our teacher got sick, the class leader had to take charge of the class meeting by himself.
我們老師生病時，班長必須獨自負責班會。
charge into the room: Ignoring the guards at the door, the angry crowd charged into the room and demanded to speak to the mayor.
不理會門口的警衛，憤怒的群眾衝進房間，要求和市長談話。
in charge of: Ms. Lin is in charge of the school's English speech contest, so please ask her if you want to join.
林老師負責學校的英語演講比賽，如果你想參加請去問她。
charm the audience: With her sweet voice and funny jokes, the young singer managed to charm the audience at the concert.
憑著甜美的歌聲和有趣的笑話，這位年輕歌手成功迷倒了演唱會的觀眾。
charm one's way into: With his friendly smile, the salesman tried to charm his way into the manager's office without an appointment.
憑著友善的笑容，這位業務員試圖在沒有預約的情況下靠魅力獲得進入經理辦公室的機會。
work like a charm: I was worried about my bad cough, but the hot ginger tea my grandma made worked like a charm.
我很擔心我嚴重的咳嗽，但奶奶泡的熱薑茶效果極佳。
chart a course: Before sailing across the ocean, the captain used maps and weather reports to chart a course for the ship.
在橫越海洋之前，船長利用地圖和氣象報告為船規劃路線。
chart the progress: The teacher uses a simple graph to chart the progress of each student's reading over the semester.
老師用一張簡單的圖表記錄每個學生這學期閱讀的進展。
chart one's own path: With nobody in her village ever going to college, she had to chart her own path without anyone to guide her.
由於她村裡從沒有人上過大學，她必須在沒有人指引的情況下走自己的路。
top the charts: The band's new song was so popular that it topped the charts for ten weeks in a row.
這個樂團的新歌非常受歡迎，連續十週登上排行榜冠軍。
cherish the memory: I will always cherish the memory of the summer we spent camping by the lake with Grandpa.
我會永遠珍藏和爺爺一起在湖邊露營的那個夏天的回憶。
cherish freedom: Having lived under strict rules in the army for years, he learned to cherish freedom and every quiet weekend at home.
在軍中嚴格的規定下生活多年後，他學會珍視自由以及在家的每個安靜週末。
cherish a hope: Although the doctors say the chance is small, the family still cherish a hope that he will wake up.
雖然醫生說機會不大，家人仍懷抱希望，相信他會醒來。
cherish one's family: After living abroad alone for years, I have learned to cherish my family and call them every week.
在國外獨自生活多年後，我學會珍惜家人，並每週打電話給他們。
